title: What If a Teaspoon of Neutron Star Landed on Earth?

scenes.text: What if a teaspoon of neutron star landed on Earth? It would weigh as much as a mountain.
A neutron star squeezes more mass than the Sun into a ball only about 30 kilometres wide.
A single teaspoon of it weighs around a billion tons, about the same as Mount Everest.
Same weight as a mountain, in something that fits on a spoon. That is how tightly the star packs its neutrons.
Its mass is more than the Sun's, squeezed into a ball about as wide as a city.
So a spoonful of the densest stuff we know weighs as much as Everest.
